chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, who said:

Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) was asked about procuring the female singer, so he said: 'The slave girl may be a distraction for the man, and her price is no more than the price of a dog, and the price of a dog is ill-gotten wealth (suh't), and the ill-gotten wealth is in the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the price of a female singer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) equates the price of a female singer to that of a dog, classifying it as 'suh't' (ill-gotten wealth) due to her role in distracting men from spiritual and moral duties. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the medium of entertainment can render earnings impure, thereby linking the acquisition of such wealth directly to the punishment of the Fire.
